records.rationale: Native qcom-pdc modular support is present through 95bf9305d2e3 and final IRQCHIP_PLATFORM_DRIVER conversion 4acd8a4be614. Keep native tristate and platform initialization/error cleanup, not the historical MODULE-only duplicate probe/IRQCHIP_DECLARE split. The whole driver/Kconfig remains LTS; no native module support is removed. No missing-consumer search is used as the sole reason; native support/history or explicit hardware/backend selection is the evidence. No hardware runtime validation.

Historical QCOM_SCM || !QCOM_SCM linkage constraint was superseded as the PDC driver/dependencies evolved; current ACK and LTS QCOM_PDC stanza contain no SCM dependency and current driver has no qcom_scm call. Preserve final native stanza, not an old forced linkage relation. No missing-consumer search is used as the sole reason; native support/history or explicit hardware/backend selection is the evidence. No hardware runtime validation.

This patch actually selects QCOM_SCM to repair an intermediate arm64 allmodconfig, despite the title wording. 0ec8b4c6469e explicitly undoes that selection, and final native/ACK PDC stanza has no SCM relation. Do not force an unrelated firmware provider. No missing-consumer search is used as the sole reason; native support/history or explicit hardware/backend selection is the evidence. No hardware runtime validation.

Historical permanent-module re-add is represented by native final IRQCHIP_PLATFORM_DRIVER qcom_pdc probe and tristate Kconfig. Keep later native node handling, locking and error cleanup. No older explicit platform_driver structure is needed. No missing-consumer search is used as the sole reason; native support/history or explicit hardware/backend selection is the evidence. No hardware runtime validation.

Retirement of intermediate select QCOM_SCM is retained in final native PDC configuration; its replacement optional dependency was itself later superseded. Do not recreate either old constraint. Native driver/Kconfig equal LTS. No missing-consumer search is used as the sole reason; native support/history or explicit hardware/backend selection is the evidence. No hardware runtime validation.

Native a947aa00edd4 provides Meson GPIO IRQ modular support with IRQCHIP_PLATFORM_DRIVER; current driver and Kconfig are exactly LTS. Do not replay old devm/remove/probe ownership implementation over native cleanup and current raw-spinlock behavior. No missing-consumer search is used as the sole reason; native support/history or explicit hardware/backend selection is the evidence. No hardware runtime validation.

This revert explicitly makes way for native Meson modular support. Keep current native tristate/platform helper, not the temporary bool/IRQCHIP_DECLARE state. Positive native replacement history and exact final files establish the disposition. No missing-consumer search is used as the sole reason; native support/history or explicit hardware/backend selection is the evidence. No hardware runtime validation.

Old GICv3 syscore-resume hook was explicitly removed in 3d41a21a35d3; it addresses ARM distributor MMIO, not the x86 SDK APIC. Keep native GIC file/header and omit this ARM-only header/export/registration. Generic PM and wakeup reporting remain separately retained. No missing-consumer search is used as the sole reason; native support/history or explicit hardware/backend selection is the evidence. No hardware runtime validation.

GICv3 initial affinity/routing callbacks mutate ARM distributor IROUTER values. Historical hooks were removed and later changed to a restricted interface. No version is needed for the selected x86 APIC backend; native ARM code remains LTS and no stub Android export is added solely for a future target. No missing-consumer search is used as the sole reason; native support/history or explicit hardware/backend selection is the evidence. No hardware runtime validation.

Public gic_resume function/export/!PM stub were part of the later explicitly removed GICv3 resume-hook path. They do not implement generic system resume. Omit ARM-only API while preserving native driver and all x86 PM paths. No missing-consumer search is used as the sole reason; native support/history or explicit hardware/backend selection is the evidence. No hardware runtime validation.

Extending the GICv3 affinity hook with force and distributor MMIO base remains ARM-only routing customization. The later restricted replacement is likewise outside the SDK x86 target; keep native GIC implementation without either old source callback signature. No missing-consumer search is used as the sole reason; native support/history or explicit hardware/backend selection is the evidence. No hardware runtime validation.

Preserve native GICv3 implementation without the retired resume/affinity hooks, old export and GIC-specific unexpected-wakeup reporting. Later ARM re-adds are independently omitted for target scope. This is not a claim that ACK permanently removed every GIC hook; x86 generic wakeup reporting and IRQ customization are separate. No missing-consumer search is used as the sole reason; native support/history or explicit hardware/backend selection is the evidence. No hardware runtime validation.

GICv2 post-affinity hook exposes ARM CPU-target map/MMIO register after native affinity update. SDK selects x86 local/I/O APIC and cannot execute this ARM driver. Omit only this driver-specific declaration/export/callsite; native generic IRQ interfaces remain. No missing-consumer search is used as the sole reason; native support/history or explicit hardware/backend selection is the evidence. No hardware runtime validation.

GICv3 re-add provides initial routing hook and restricted affinity callback with distributor/redistributor addresses/stride. These parameters and callsites are ARM controller-specific, not generic IRQ policy. Omit for current x86 SDK without declaring the hardware feature unnecessary on ARM. No missing-consumer search is used as the sole reason; native support/history or explicit hardware/backend selection is the evidence. No hardware runtime validation.

GICv3 suspend hook plus public distributor/CPU initialization and write-pending exports support ARM controller suspend policy. Omit the entire target-specific dependency chain, including syscore registration and renamed public helpers, while retaining native LTS bodies and x86 suspend infrastructure. No missing-consumer search is used as the sole reason; native support/history or explicit hardware/backend selection is the evidence. No hardware runtime validation.

ITS save/disable and restore/enable exports are ARM GIC interrupt-translation service helpers for platform S2IDLE. Native private implementations remain; no ARM-only source API is added solely for future hardware. x86 APIC/MSI and generic PM are unaffected. No missing-consumer search is used as the sole reason; native support/history or explicit hardware/backend selection is the evidence. No hardware runtime validation.

Apple AIC firmware-specifier affinity callback is selected only with ARM64 and ARCH_APPLE/COMPILE_TEST. The patch adds a controller-specific get_fwspec_info implementation, not a generic firmware ABI. Retain native AIC file under x86 SDK target scope; no Apple hardware support is required here. No missing-consumer search is used as the sole reason; native support/history or explicit hardware/backend selection is the evidence. No hardware runtime validation.

source_limits: Local patches contain lore URLs, not opened. Exclusions address controller-specific MMIO/CPU contracts and selected architecture, not unproven absence of userspace demand. Mixed merge candidates with other subsystems remain pending.
